Article Title: NPF gets most, BJP second as 111 MPs, MLAs switch parties since 2022: ADR
Article Text:
At least 111 sitting MPs and MLAs changed political parties after being elected between 2022 and 2026

NPF received most lawmakers, BJP second

Who were the 29 lawmakers who joined BJP?

Nagaland, West Bengal account for major share of cases

NDPP, AITC and Congress recorded most exits

Not all 111 cases were individual defections

ADR cautions that list may not be exhaustive

NEW DELHI: At least 111 sitting MPs and MLAs changed political parties after being elected between 2022 and 2026, according to an analysis by the Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) and National Election Watch (NEW). The report, released on September 24, covers elections and by-elections held during the period and includes 26 Lok Sabha MPs, seven Rajya Sabha MPs and 78 MLAs.The cases span 17 states and Union Territories, with Nagaland recording the highest number at 32, followed by West Bengal with 20, Telangana with nine, and Goa and Punjab with eight each. Maharashtra and Meghalaya recorded six cases each, Manipur five, Arunachal Pradesh and Gujarat four each, Himachal Pradesh and Rajasthan two each, while Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi recorded one each.Of the 111 lawmakers, 32 joined the Naga People's Front (NPF), accounting for 29 per cent of the total. The BJP received 29, or 26 per cent, followed by the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) with 20, or 18 per cent.The Congress received nine lawmakers, or 8 per cent, while Shiv Sena received eight, or 7 per cent. NPP received six, or 5 per cent, and the People's Party of Arunachal (PPA) received four, or 4 per cent.Together, NPF, BJP and NCPI accounted for 81 of the 111 lawmakers, or 73 per cent.The NPF's figure was largely linked to the political realignment involving the Nationalist Democratic Progressive Party (NDPP) and NPF in Nagaland. ADR classifies party mergers separately from individual defections, making the distinction important when reading the overall figures.Of the 29 lawmakers listed as having joined the BJP, seven were Rajya Sabha MPs and 22 were MLAs. No Lok Sabha MP in the ADR dataset moved to the BJP.The seven Rajya Sabha MPs were originally elected from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP): Swati Maliwal, Ashok Mittal, Harbhajan Singh, Raghav Chadha, Sandeep Kumar Pathak, Vikramjit Singh Sahney and Rajinder Gupta. The seven AAP MPs subsequently joined the BJP in April 2026.Among the MLAs were eight Congress legislators from Goa, four Congress legislators from Gujarat and two from Himachal Pradesh. The report also lists five JD(U) MLAs from Manipur as having moved to the BJP.Other BJP entrants included Samajwadi Party MLA Manoj Kumar Pandey from Uttar Pradesh, Congress MLA Nirmala Sapre from Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka MLA G Janardhan Reddy, whose Kalyana Rajya Pragathi Paksha (KRPP) merged with the BJP, according to the ADR analysis.Four Gujarat Congress MLAs, CJ Chavda, Arjun Modhwadia, Arvind Ladani and Chirag Patel, resigned, joined the BJP and subsequently contested by-elections.Nagaland recorded 32 cases, all involving MLAs. The cases were largely linked to the NDPP-NPF realignment, with 25 representatives originally elected from the NDPP among those who changed parties and 32 lawmakers joining the NPF.West Bengal recorded 20 cases, all involving Lok Sabha MPs. All 20 were originally elected on AITC tickets and subsequently moved to the NCPI, according to the analysis. The MPs have claimed a merger with the NCPI, with the matter pending before Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla.Telangana recorded nine cases, all involving MLAs originally elected from the BRS, while Congress emerged as the principal recipient. Goa recorded eight cases involving Congress MLAs who moved to the BJP. Punjab also recorded eight cases, including six Rajya Sabha members and two MLAs.Maharashtra recorded six cases, all involving Lok Sabha MPs elected from Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) who subsequently moved to Shiv Sena led by Eknath Shinde. Meghalaya recorded six MLA cases, while Manipur recorded five.Among the parties from which lawmakers moved, NDPP recorded the highest number of exits, with 25, or 23 per cent of the total. AITC followed with 20, or 18 per cent, while Congress accounted for 19, or 17 per cent.BRS recorded nine exits, or 8 per cent. AAP and NCP each accounted for seven, or 6 per cent, while Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) accounted for six, or 5 per cent. JD(U) recorded five, or 5 per cent, and NPP four, or 4 per cent.Together, NDPP, AITC and Congress accounted for 64 of the 111 lawmakers who changed parties, or 58 per cent.ADR's analysis divides the 111 cases into four categories based on how the change took place.The first covers individual switches or defections, where a legislator voluntarily leaves one party and joins another without resigning from the House.The second covers party mergers, where the original party or a substantial section of its legislative wing formally merges with another party, such as the NDPP-NPF case in Nagaland.The third covers resignation followed by a by-election, where a legislator resigns from the Assembly or Parliament, joins another party and subsequently contests and wins a by-election.The fourth covers disqualification followed by a by-election, where a member is disqualified under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution, later joins another party and wins the seat again through a by-election.ADR also noted that recent defections had been associated with the fall of governments in some State Assemblies.ADR and NEW said they made every effort to identify and include all relevant cases but cautioned that the list may not be exhaustive because of the lack of systematically maintained and readily accessible official data on lawmakers changing political parties. Other relevant cases may therefore not have been included.The previous ADR report on MPs and MLAs who changed parties was released on September 9, 2021, and covered the period from 2014 to 2021.
Article Summary: At least 111 sitting mps and mlas changed political parties after being elected between 2022 and 2026. Nagaland recorded the highest number at 32, followed by west bengal with 20, telangana with nine, and goa and punjab with eight each. Not all 111 cases were individual defections.

Article Title: Vijay government exempts Tamil Nadu Public (Law & Order) department from RTI- what it means
Article Text:
Tamil Nadu CM C Joseph Vijay

What the exemption means

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Tamil Nadu government led by CM C Joseph Vijay has exempted the Public (Law and Order) Department from the ambit of the Right to Information (RTI) Act, classifying it as an Intelligence and Security Organisation under Section 24(4) of the law.A Gazette notification issued by the state government places the department under the exemption framework applicable to intelligence and security organisations. The move means information held by the department will generally be outside the scope of RTI requests, subject to the statutory exceptions under the Act.The Public (Law and Order) Department deals with matters concerning policing, public order and law-and-order administration and RTI Act is a law to provide for setting out the practical regime of right to information for citizens wherein they can secure access to information under the control of public authorities.This exemption could therefore affect RTI requests seeking information relating to communal incidents, political agitations, police actions and other law-and-order matters handled by the department.The statement reads, "Gazette notification dated September 21, 2026, issued by the Human Resources Management Department, the Governor, exercising powers under Section 24(4) of the Right to Information Act, 2005, has specified the Public (Law and Order) Department as an "Intelligence and Security Organization" established by the Tamil Nadu government, "for which the said Act shall not apply."However, Section 24 of the RTI Act does not provide a blanket exemption. Even organisations covered by the provision are required to provide information relating to allegations of corruption and human-rights violations, subject to the procedure prescribed under the law.Tamil Nadu has previously used the provision to exclude organisations including the Tamil Nadu State Vigilance Commission and the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption.
Article Summary: Tamil nadu government exempts public (law and order) department from the ambit of the right to information (rti) act. The department is classified as an intelligence and security organisation under section 24(4) of the law. The move means information held by the department will generally be outside the scope of rti requests.

Article Title: Amit Shah flags off India's first LNG train in Gujarat, launches Rs 1,542 crore railway projects
Article Text:
File photo: Amit Shah launches rail projects worth over Rs 1,542 Cr, flag off India's first LNG-powered train in Gujarat

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Union home and cooperation minister Amit Shah on Sunday flagged off India’s first LNG-powered train in Gujarat and launched a series of railway projects worth more than Rs 1,542 crore at Sabarmati The LNG-based train uses a diesel-LNG dual-fuel system, with two 1,400 HP Driving Power Cars at the Sabarmati Integrated Coaching Depot converted to run on both fuels. LNG can replace nearly 40 per cent of diesel consumption under the system.The initiative is aimed at reducing diesel use and fuel costs while lowering emissions including carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter.The train was among several railway projects launched by Shah in Sabarmati, with the package also focusing on railway safety, line capacity and freight operations.Shah also laid the foundation stone for the indigenous Kavach automatic train protection system across 404 km of railway network in the Ahmedabad division.The project, estimated to cost around Rs 411 crore, covers 157 km of the Ahmedabad-Palanpur section and 247 km of the Ahmedabad-Samakhiyali section. Kavach is designed to help prevent train collisions, protect against overspeeding and reduce risks linked to human error.An automatic block signalling system has also been introduced across 122.57 km of railway sections between Sabarmati-Kalol-Bhandu Motidau and Sabarmati-Sanand-Jakhwada at a cost of around Rs 118.83 crore. The system is designed to maintain safe distances between trains and increase route capacity.Shah also inaugurated the WAG-12 locomotive maintenance shed at Sabarmati, built at an estimated cost of Rs 700 crore.The facility will provide maintenance for 300 high-horsepower WAG-12 electric locomotives, which have a capacity of around 12,000 HP and are designed to haul heavy and long freight trains.The Sabarmati-Sarkhej railway line doubling project, estimated at Rs 313.27 crore, will cover a 21-km stretch and is targeted for completion by March 2028.The project covers stations including Sabarmati, Gandhigram, Vastrapur and Sarkhej and includes bridges and road underpasses.The doubling is expected to improve train movement and connectivity towards the Sarkhej-Dholera region while supporting industrial and commercial activity in the area.The projects launched in Gujarat are aimed at improving railway safety, increasing operational capacity and promoting alternative-fuel technology in rail transport.
Article Summary: Union home and cooperation minister amit shah on sunday flagged off india’s first lng-powered train in gujarat. Shah also launched a series of railway projects worth more than rs 1,542 crore at sabarmati. The projects are aimed at improving railway safety, increasing operational capacity and promoting alternative-fuel technology in rail transport.

Article Title: Bengal SIR row: CM Suvendu Adhikari pins blame on Mamata for deletion of 27 lakh voters
Article Text:
Adhikari claimed the deletions were ordered by judicial officers in a case filed by Banerjee herself.

Politics over voter rolls

Questions over election commission

West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari has blamed former CM Mamata Banerjee for the deletion of around 27 lakh names from the state’s electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), rejecting allegations that the BJP or the Election Commission was responsible.Adhikari claimed the deletions were ordered by judicial officers following directions from the Supreme Court in a case filed by Banerjee herself. He accused the TMC leader of trying to shift responsibility after her defeat in the Assembly elections.“The responsibility for the deletion of 27 lakh names lies with Mamata Banerjee, not the BJP or the Election Commission. Judicial officers took the decision following the Supreme Court's directions in a case filed by her,” Adhikari said at a press conference.The Election Commission has said 22.21 lakh of the deleted voters had filed appeals seeking their names to be restored. More than 38 lakh appeals have been filed in total against both exclusions and inclusions during the SIR process.The SIR exercise has become a major political flashpoint in Bengal. The TMC has alleged that genuine voters were removed from the rolls and has demanded that their names be restored.Adhikari, meanwhile, sought to contrast Bengal with Kerala, where the revision exercise has also taken place.“If SIR is good in Kerala, why is it bad in West Bengal? We have won 208 seats, while the two sides (TMC and its allies) have 80. Mamata Banerjee is unable to accept the people's verdict,” he said.His comments came a day after Banerjee addressed a rally in Serampore and renewed her criticism of the Election Commission and the BJP over the voter-roll revision.Adhikari also referred to a meeting between Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.He said the meeting and the poll panel’s subsequent statement showed that decisions concerning Bengal’s SIR were not taken by the CEC alone.The issue comes amid scrutiny of the functioning of the three-member Election Commission. An Indian Express investigation reported that the two election commissioners had raised objections on several occasions over decisions linked to the SIR exercise.The Election Commission has maintained that differences during internal discussions are normal and that its final decisions on the exercise were unanimous.
Article Summary: Adhikari claimed the deletions were ordered by judicial officers in a case filed by banerjee herself. He accused the tmc leader of trying to shift responsibility after her defeat in the assembly elections. More than 38 lakh appeals have been filed against both exclusions and inclusions during the sir process.

Article Title: PM Modi recalls 2016 surgical strikes on Mann Ki Baat, says terrorism will get decisive response
Article Text:
File photo: PM Modi in 'Mann Ki Baat'

Other highlights from Mann Ki Baat

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday recalled the 2016 surgical strikes carried out by the Indian Army across the Line of Control (LoC), saying India has made it clear that terrorism will be met with a “strong and decisive response”.Addressing the 138th episode of his monthly radio programme Mann Ki Baat , PM Modi said the surgical strikes, carried out on September 28-29, 2016, demonstrated India's resolve to respond to cross-border terrorism.“A major historical achievement of India is set to complete 10 years in just a day—the surgical strike. Ten years ago, on September 28–29, 2016, the Indian Army conducted a surgical strike on terrorist hideouts in PoJK. The world was astonished by the manner in which our brave soldiers crossed the Line of Control (LoC) to take action against terrorism,” he said.PM Modi said the operation had demonstrated a new approach to India's counter-terrorism policy.“The surgical strike boldly demonstrated a new example of India's counter-terrorism policy to the entire world. It served as our decisive response to the long-standing suffering India had endured due to terrorist attacks,” he said.“India has made it clear that terrorism will be met with a strong and decisive response,” PM Modi added.The Prime Minister also referred to the Balakot airstrike and Operation Sindoor, saying India had repeatedly sent the same message in response to terrorism.“Over the past decade, from the Balakot airstrike to 'Operation Sindoor', India has repeatedly sent a clear message: if terrorists dare to cast a hostile eye on India, they will face a befitting response,” he said.PM Modi also asserted that India was following a policy of “zero tolerance against terrorism”.The surgical strikes were carried out in response to the 2016 Uri terror attack, with the Indian Army targeting terror launch pads across the LoC.The Prime Minister also referred to the ongoing Census exercise, describing it as a “national responsibility” and saying every citizen had a role to play. He said the first phase of the Census was almost complete across all states and Union territories, with information on more than 32 crore families already recorded. He urged people to actively participate in the exercise and make use of the online enumeration facility.With October 2 approaching, PM Modi also highlighted cleanliness initiatives being carried out by communities across the country and recalled Mahatma Gandhi's emphasis on cleanliness.“October 2nd is just a few days away; it is the birth anniversary of Revered Bapu. Bapu gave us many mantras for life; cleanliness is one of them,” he said.PM Modi cited examples of youngsters cleaning a river in Madhya Pradesh, restoring old stepwells and wells in Andhra Pradesh, volunteers cleaning Mumbai beaches and young people in Delhi spreading awareness about waste segregation. He also mentioned students and local residents in West Bengal who were cleaning picnic spots.“One thing is clearly evident in all these efforts: it started with one person, then others joined in and the caravan grew. This is public participation,” PM Modi said.“Cleanliness is also the most beautiful tribute we can pay to Bapu,” he added.PM Modi also spoke about the fight against narcotics and said young people were coming together to spread awareness against drug addiction through the Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan. He said millions of young people had taken a pledge to stay away from drugs and had also taken responsibility for spreading the message among others.The Prime Minister also recalled the history of the Somnath temple, saying those who sought to erase India's identity by destroying it ultimately had no existence. He said the temple continued to stand in its grandeur by the sea, blessing India with immortality.During the broadcast, PM Modi also paid tribute to late VHP leader Ashok Singhal on his birth anniversary, recalling his contribution to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement and describing his life as that of an ascetic who remained engaged with society.
Article Summary: Prime minister narendra modi recalled the 2016 surgical strikes carried out by the indian army across the line of control (loc) he said the operation demonstrated india's resolve to respond to cross-border terrorism. Pm modi also referred to the balakot airstrike and operation sindoor, saying india had repeatedly sent the same message.

Article Text:
EC issues clarification amid SIR row

EC clarifies officer, IT division row

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Saturday said all decisions taken on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, including the nationwide exercise, were approved unanimously, while announcing measures to simplify the process for voters facing notices over discrepancies.The clarification comes amid row over report that claimed differences within the EC over SIR of electoral rolls."In the recent months, the Commission has taken numerous decisions including SIR across the country. The order for the SIR issued on 24.6.2025 for all the States/UTs, starting with Bihar, followed by West Bengal and 30 other States/UTs was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. The same has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India vide its order dated 27.5.2026. The schedule for SIR for 12 States and UTs was issued on 27.10.2025 and those for 19 States/UTs was issued on 14.05.2026 with the unanimous approval of the Commission. The final figure of number of electors will be known only after final publication in the remaining 12 states of Phase-III," the poll body said in a statement.At a meeting held on Saturday, the Commission decided that voters who receive notices during the ongoing SIR over being unmapped or having logical discrepancies will not ordinarily have to appear before the electoral registration officer (ERO).Booth-level officers (BLOs) will visit their homes to collect documents and upload them on ECINet for the ERO to decide.Hearings will be held only in exceptional cases, preferably online. An adult family member can also attend a hearing on behalf of the elector if authorised. The Commission said facilities for online hearings would be strengthened.The Commission also directed district election officers to set up help desks and special camps for people living in night shelters, labourers, poor people and homeless persons, depending on local requirements.The EC said SIR has been completed in 20 states and Union territories, including Bihar and West Bengal. It said voters whose names were left out during or after the exercise, as well as young and first-time voters, can apply to the concerned ERO for inclusion through continuous updation. Chief Electoral Officers (CEOs), DEOs and EROs have been directed to launch a special enrolment drive.The Commission also clarified that a letter sent to the Cabinet Secretary was not related to any policy decision concerning the Commission or its IT division, but concerned the functioning of an officer on deputation to the EC.It said work redistribution orders issued by the officer were not implemented after directions from two Commissioners, and oversight of the IT division by the Deputy Election Commissioner was never withdrawn.The EC said field officers have role-based access to the ECINet system based on their statutory powers. A committee headed by a senior Deputy Election Commissioner and including an independent IIT/IIIT expert will review the system for compliance with relevant laws and rules.The Commission also said future initiatives involving IT modules and portals would be discussed by the Committee of Officers before being placed for approval.The Commission extended the deadline for filing claims and objections in Delhi till October 30, following a request from the Delhi CEO. The deadline for disposal of notices and claims and objections has been extended till November 30.In Maharashtra, the deadline for filing claims and objections has been extended till October 12, while their disposal will continue till November 10.The Commission further said the SIR order issued on June 24, 2025, covering all states and UTs and subsequently implemented in phases, had received unanimous approval. It added that the Supreme Court upheld the order on May 27, 2026.In Goa, the EC said BLOs had been directed to visit voters left out of the rolls and collect their forms. Of 97 such voters, 81 have already filled Form 6 for inclusion.The Commission also directed that agendas for its meetings be circulated in advance and minutes issued, while requiring officers' annual performance reports to be completed by December 31 each year. It further said Commission approval would be required for official foreign trips and that directions issued by Commissioners to officers must be complied with.
Article Summary: Ec issues clarification amid sir row. Claims deadline extended in delhi, maharashtra. Election commission says all decisions taken on the special intensive revision (sir) of electoral rolls, including the nationwide exercise, were approved unanimously. Ec announces measures to simplify the process for voters facing notices over discrepancies.

Article Title: Kharge, Sonia and Rahul pay homage to late PM Manmohan Singh
Article Text:
Congress leaders paid homage to former PM Manmohan Singh

NEW DELHI: Remembering him as a statesman and a visionary, Congress netas Mallikarjun Kharge Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi Saturday led the party in paying homage to late Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on his birth anniversary.Congress held a ceremony at the party office where the Gandhis, senior functionaries and office-bearers paid floral tributes to Singh. Article Title: J&K BJP bigwig meets Shah day after Omar moves statehood resolution with autonomy reference
Article Text:
Sunil Sharma meets HM Amit Shah in New Delhi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: A day after CM Omar Abdullah moved an assembly resolution for restoration of J&K’s statehood with a reference to a similar document of the year 2000 on autonomy, BJP leader of opposition Sunil Sharma met Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday for “advice” even as PDP upped the ante and sought an amendment to condemn Article 370’s abrogation.Vowing to block the resolution, Sharma said Shah “reaffirmed the Union govt’s unwavering commitment to peace, development and prosperity of Jammu and Kashmir”.Sharma made it clear that BJP was prepared to debate the statehood restoration document brought by the Omar-led National Conference (NC) govt but would not accept attempts to “smuggle in” issues of Article 370 and the 2000 autonomy resolution.“When the (Omar-led) govt has lost its strength on governance, an attempt is being made to recover that by invoking references designed to stir emotion among the people of Kashmir. At no cost will the so-called autonomy resolution or Article 370 be allowed to become part of this debate,” Sharma said.PDP would have none of it. It called Friday’s resolution “weak” and demanded that the document begin with a denunciation of Article 370’s revocation by the Centre on Aug 5, 2019. PDP legislator Muntazir Mehdi disclosed that he had moved an amendment calling on the House to “express its deep anguish over the unilateral measures” of 2019 and urging the Centre to ensure “immediate restoration of J&K’s full statehood along with its constitutional safeguards”.Omar had moved the resolution amid a BJP backlash to the autonomy reference, with its members ripping up copies amid anti-national chants directed at NC. MLAs of NC ally Congress supported the resolution and confronted rivals. CPM, Peoples Conference and PDP also backed the resolution. The autonomy resolution was passed by the assembly in June 2000 when J&K was a state.Explaining the reference to previous resolutions, Omar said the aim was to convey that the House continued to stand by all past decisions. He rejected BJP’s charges, asked “how demanding statehood can be anti-national” and pointed out that statehood was a promise made by the Centre and reaffirmed by PM Narendra Modi at an event where BJP’s Sharma was present.Omar has been under pressure for months now, accused by rivals of dropping demands to restore Article 370 and demanding statehood only. On Saturday, NC spokesperson Tanvir called the resolution a powerful reminder that the party had “not forgotten” its agenda. BJP MLA Devyani Rana accused NC of raking up 25-year-old autonomy demands on the pretext of statehood.
Article Summary: Sunil sharma meets hm amit shah in new delhi for ‘advice’ on j&k statehood. Sharma said shah “reaffirmed the union govt’s unwavering commitment to peace, development and prosperity of jammu and kashmir”

Article Title: 2 more Naga men killed as ethnic violence flares up in Manipur again
Article Text:
Manipur violence claims another life as gunmen strike Senapati village

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Two Mao Naga men were shot dead by unidentified gunmen at Kalenjang village in Manipur's Senapati district Saturday afternoon, with two others wounded, in the latest escalation in a Naga-Kuki conflict that has claimed more than 40 lives since Feb.The shooting took place under Senapati police station around 2.30pm, shortly after CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh left a function about 30km away. It came two days after four Tangkhul Naga men were killed allegedly by Myanmar-based Kuki National Army-Burma (B) at Pilong village near the international border in Kamjong district.The Kalenjang and Pilong killings are part of a series of Naga-Kuki clashes that began in Feb, shortly after Singh's govt took charge. At least 21 people - 11 Nagas and 10 Kukis, including a pregnant woman - have been killed since Aug 27. The toll is separate from the Meitei-Kuki conflict, which has killed over 300.Both the communities have accused militant groups from the other side of the attacks. Police have said several such allegations are under investigation and have not been independently verified.The killings came as United Naga Council (UNC), the apex body of Naga tribes in Manipur, called off its 131-day economic blockade of NH-2 and NH-37 after a meeting with home ministry and Manipur govt at the BSF Frontier headquarters in Guwahati Saturday.The blockade followed the abduction of six Liangmai Naga civilians in Kangpokpi district.Manipur Congress president Okram Ibobi Singh accused BJP-headed NDA govts in the state and Centre of remaining "silent spectators" to civilian killings. "Govt is behaving as if it is not concerned about the killings of civilians of any community," the former three-time CM said. "We strongly condemn the killings of innocent civilians from Naga, Kuki and Meitei communities," he said, while questioning security along the Myanmar border.
Article Summary: Manipur violence claims another life as gunmen strike senapati village. At least 21 people - 11 nagas and 10 kukis, including a pregnant woman - have been killed since aug 27. The toll is separate from the meitei-kuki conflict, which has killed over 300.

Article Title: PM Modi, HM Shah put CEC in charge of match-fixing elections: Rahul Gandhi
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi calls CEC Gyanesh Kumar a ‘BJP headhunter’

NEW DELHI: With a top former bureaucrat of Kerala reportedly saying that chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had approached him to contest election on BJP ticket, leader of the opposition Rahul Gandhi Saturday mocked that the poll panel chief was a headhunter for BJP and then put in charge of fixing polls."First, Gyanesh Kumar - then a serving IAS officer - was used to recruit for BJP. Then PM Modi and Shah made him the umpire and put him in charge of match-fixing India's elections," the Congress functionary posted on X, referring to the media reports.Meanwhile, Congress spokesperson Jairam Ramesh dismissed the Election Commission 's response to the recent media revelations. It has just issued a wishy-washy press note that raises further questions on its intent, integrity, impartiality and credibility."
Article Summary: Rahul gandhi calls cec gyanesh kumar a ‘bjp headhunter’ he says pm modi and shah made him the umpire and put him in charge of match-fixing. Congress spokesperson jairam ramesh dismissed the election commission's response to the recent media revelations.

Article Title: Property damaged, highway blocked: LPU campus tense over unverified rape claim - top developments

Rape claim sparks LPU unrest: Property damaged, highway blocked

Students raise grievances with university administration

Chitkara University protest a day earlier

Students at Lovely Professional University (LPU) in Punjab’s Phagwara damaged property and blocked the Jalandhar-Phagwara national highway early Sunday following unverified reports on social media about the alleged rape of a female student. Police said they had no information of any such crime.Kapurthala Senior Superintendent of Police Gaurav Toora said police received information around 1.45 am that students had gathered on the LPU campus and blocked a road. Addressing the unverified rape claim, Toora said, "When we reached here, we came to know that there were rumours. Because of the rumours, students gathered here".Videos circulating on social media showed students damaging window panes and flower pots, while some objects were also seen being set on fire. The students also blocked the Jalandhar-Phagwara national highway.Toora said police spoke to students who raised issues with the LPU administration and that efforts were being made to address their concerns."We spoke to students who had some issues with the LPU administration.We heard them and are trying to get them resolved. The situation is completely under control," the SSP said.He added that students told police their grievances were not being addressed properly. An assessment of the property damage is under way, and necessary legal action will be taken, Toora said.A heavy police force has been deployed at the university, with police stating that the situation is now under control.The incident came a day after students at Chitkara University in Patiala held a protest following unverified claims on social media that two female students had allegedly died by suicide on the campus. Students had also damaged a police vehicle during that protest.
Article Summary: Students at lovely professional university (lpu) in punjab’s phagwara damaged property and blocked the jalandhar-phagwara national highway. Police say rumours triggered campus unrest following unverified reports on social media about the alleged rape of a female student. Police said they had no information of any such crime.

Article Title: New Form 6 enrolments where no SIR is under way won't need mapping
Article Text:
EC retains mandatory SIR declaration for fresh voter enrolment.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Those applying for fresh enrolment as electors through Form 6 in locations other than the 12 states and UTs where special intensive revision (SIR) is currently underway will no longer need to attach a declaration mapping themselves or their relative to the electoral rolls from the last SIR.In the states and UTs where SIR is going on, Form 6 will continue to be accompanied by a mandatory declaration by the applicant listing their or their relatives' electoral rolls details from the last SIR, apart from their father's, mother's and spouse's names and their respective EPIC numbers, if available.A statement put out by the three-member Election Commission Saturday justified the continued requirement of new electors to submit the declaration along with Form 6 as part of SIR, saying "the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR has been upheld by the Supreme Court ".For the non-SIR period, the forms applicable as per the Registration of Electors Rules 1960 will be used, the commission added. The declaration was first added to Form 6 in the SIR order issued for Bihar on June 24, 2025.Sources told TOI the system will revert to the pre-SIR Form 6 with immediate effect in non-SIR states/UTs, including the states due for polls early next year.As exclusively reported by TOI on Sept 25, a special summary revision will be undertaken in these poll-bound states later this year.Both election commissioners, SS Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had in May and Aug, respectively, sent internal notes to the deputy election commissioner concerned, opining that Form 6 can only be amended by the govt.This was after they had approved of the declaration attached to the form as part of three SIR orders. While election commissioner Vivek Joshi raised objection to the revised Form 6 format on May 16 this year, Sandhu endorsed it on Aug 13, well after Supreme Court had upheld the SIR process. Their concerns were later echoed by opposition parties led by Congress, which alleged that Form 6 was changed "unilaterally" by CEC Gyanesh Kumar.The EC statement Saturday, however, put on record that all three SIR orders - issued on June 24, 2025, for Phase 1 Bihar; on Oct 27, 2025, for Phase 2 in 12 states; and on May 14, 2026, for the ongoing Phase 3 in 19 states/UTs - were unanimously approved by the CEC and the two commissioners.To eliminate any scope for doubt, EC added Saturday's statement was also issued with the "approval of the full commission".The declaration required to be attached to Form 6 itself has undergone a change since it was introduced in the SIR order for Bihar. The Bihar declaration required those seeking fresh enrolment to declare their or their parents' date and place of birth and submit proof of the same from the list of 11 documents attached to the SIR order, though this list was not exhaustive. This declaration was revised for subsequent phases of SIR, introducing mapping to the last SIR instead of seeking proof of citizenship.
Article Summary: Ec retains mandatory sir declaration for fresh voter enrolment. Sources told toi the system will revert to the pre-sir form 6 with immediate effect in non-sir states/uts, including the states due for polls early next year. A special summary revision will be undertaken in these poll-bound states later this year.

NEW DELHI: National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) Thursday declared NEET-PG 2026 result, with 2,65,960 candidates having appeared in the exam held in two phases this year. NEET-PG was conducted on Aug 30 for admission to MD, MS, DNB, DrNB Direct 6-year courses and PG Medical Diploma courses for 2026-27.NBEMS said NEET-PG rank represents overall merit position of a candidate among those who appeared for the exam and is based on actual marks scored and applicable tie-breaking criteria. The board also said each question in both papers was reviewed by faculty members from the specialty areas and none was found to be technically incorrect. Scorecards can be downloaded from NBEMS website on or after Oct 1. The answer key will be published on or after Oct 1.

Article Title: ‘Old footage’: Delhi Police fact-checks viral Jantar Mantar protest video amid SIR row
Article Text:
Debunked viral footage being circulated on social media

Protests over SIR row

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has debunked viral visuals of a massive protest being shared on social media, citing that it contains old footage from Jantar Mantar. They have also warned that legal action could be taken against those deliberately spreading misleading content.A video is currently being circulated on social media as showing a live, massive protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar. The video was shared by several accounts on X, including Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut, who claimed that protests against Kumar had begun in Delhi.Raut had shared the video with a caption saying, “Protests against Gyanesh Kumar Hatao have begun in Delhi, today's Jantar Mantar scene... A fight to the finish!”The DCP New Delhi account on Saturday called the claim “false” and said the footage was “archived material from a past event”.“The claim of a live, massive protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar today is false. The Video is Old: The footage being shared is archived material from a past event,” the Delhi Police said in a post on X.The police also warned that legal action would be taken against those found deliberately spreading misinformation or circulating misleading content.The video surfaced amid a widening political row over the Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for Kumar’s resignation.The controversy intensified after a report said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months on decisions and procedures linked to the SIR exercise.Opposition parties have questioned the conduct of the revision and alleged irregularities, while the Election Commission has rejected the allegations.The Election Commission said on Saturday that decisions taken on SIR, including the nationwide exercise, were approved unanimously by the three-member poll panel. It also clarified that a letter sent to the Cabinet Secretary concerned the functioning of an officer on deputation and was not related to any policy decision of the Commission.The poll panel also announced measures to ease the process for voters who receive notices over discrepancies, including allowing booth-level officers to visit their homes to collect documents and providing online hearings in exceptional cases. It said voters left out of the rolls, as well as young and first-time voters, can seek inclusion through the continuous updation process.The clarification over the viral video comes as opposition-led protests against the Election Commission have continued.The Indian Youth Congress marched from Raisina Road to Jantar Mantar on Friday as part of a nationwide programme demanding Kumar’s resignation. Meanwhile, Peoples Democratic Party chief Mehbooba Mufti has called for a protest at Jantar Mantar on September 29, asking people to join a demonstration centred on democratic and secular values.The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has also threatened nationwide protests from October 2 if Kumar does not resign. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said the agitation would begin in Mumbai on Gandhi Jayanti and then move to other cities.Opposition parties are also expected to discuss the SIR exercise and the functioning of the Election Commission at an INDIA bloc meeting on September 30.
Article Summary: Debunked viral footage being circulated on social media as showing a massive protest against chief election commissioner gyanesh kumar. The video was shared by several accounts on x, including shiv sena (ubt) mp sanjay raut, who claimed that protests against kumar had begun in delhi.

Article Title: After meeting, EC says officials will visit homes of those sent notices
Article Text:
ECINET software to be audited after complaints​

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A full meeting of the Election Commission of India on Saturday - the first after reports of alleged internal differences - decided to exempt electors who have got notices for being unmapped to the last SIR or over logical discrepancies, from hearings by electoral registration officer (ERO) or assistant EROs. Instead, EROs and AEROs will visit homes of such electors to collect documents that would then be uploaded to ECINet for a final decision by the ERO.The EC also agreed to an independent audit of ECINET software though it rejected allegations that EROs were being locked out."Only in exceptional circumstances, as decided by the ERO, hearing will be held, preferably online. Any adult member of the family can be authorised by the elector to attend the hearing on their behalf, if required," the EC said in a statement after the meeting attended by CEC Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.EC also agreed to an independent audit of ECINET software even as it rejected allegations that booth-level officers and EROs were being kept out.Facilities for online hearing will be strengthened, while DEOs will create enough help desks and hold special camps for the poor, labourers, homeless people, and those in night shelters.The relief for electors who received notices under SIR follows criticism from affected voters and opposition that genuine citizens are being inconvenienced by discrepancies flagged by ECINET.These include name or gender mismatch; less than a 15-year gap with a parent; less than a 40-year gap with a grandparent; being one of six progeny mapped to the same parent; and less than a nine-month gap between siblings.Until now, notice recipients had to appear before the ERO at the specified time and place with documents proving eligibility to remain on the rolls. With large numbers of notices in states like Delhi, including to prominent persons, many said citizens were forced to run around to retain voting rights.EC has also denied reports that field officers were locked out of ECINET, saying role-based access exists, but agreed to an independent audit. A senior DEC-led panel will review ECINET to double-check that it complies with the provisions of the Acts and rules and submit a report to EC.
Article Summary: Ec also agreed to an independent audit of ecinet software though it rejected allegations that eros were being locked out.facilities for online hearing will be strengthened, while deos will create enough help desks and hold special camps for poor, labourers, homeless people.

Article Title: ‘All SIR rollout decisions unanimous’: EC says agendas for all meetings to be circulated in advance
Article Text:
EC says SIR decisions taken unanimously by full commission

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Election Commission asserted Saturday that the decisions regarding special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls were taken unanimously by chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.The statement came following the first meeting of the "full" Commission after a report in The Indian Express suggested the CEC disregarded the views of the two ECs on SIR-related calls, which sparked a political row, with the opposition targeting the govt and the CEC."The order for SIR issued on 24.6.2025 for all States/UTs, starting with Bihar, followed by West Bengal and 30 other States/UTs was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission," the EC said.It also denied the claim that Sandhu and Joshi wrote to the Cabinet secretary to flag concerns over policy matters or IT processes.SIR has been implemented in 20 states and UTs and is under way in 12 others. The poll panel also refuted the claim that Sandhu and Joshi wrote separate letters to the cabinet secretary to flag their concerns about policy matters or processes adopted by EC's IT division over which they no longer had control.The letter was "related to the work of an officer on deputation to EC. The work re-distribution orders issued by the officer concerned were not actually implemented after the orders of the two commissioners and the oversight over the IT division by the DEC was never actually withdrawn," EC said.The report said Sandhu and Joshi had called the move "a clear violation" of the law that governs EC and sought action against senior DEC Maneesh Garg, and linked the commissioners' objections to field officers allegedly being locked out of ECINET making it a "centralised" software directly controlled by EC.The allegations linking the commissioners' objections to SIR and alleged lack of access to field officers to ECINET were seized upon by opposition to point their guns at the CEC. LoP Rahul Gandhi demanded he be imprisoned while opposition appeared set to seek his removal afresh.Saturday's full commission meeting and the statement issued later sought to fix this; it cleared the air point by point, besides conveying the message that the three members had resolved their internal issues.EC decided to concede on a slew of matters raised by the commissioners through internal notes, deciding that the agenda for all meetings shall henceforth be circulated in advance and the minutes issued. Also, annual performance appraisal reports of all officers would be completed by Dec 31 every year. The statement said all directions issued by the commissioners to the officers of the commission will be complied with and foreign trips for officers approved by the full commission.On opposition's claim of disenfranchisement of 13 crore voters in SIR, EC said the final figure of electors will be known only after final publication of the roll in the remaining 12 states of Phase 3.
Article Summary: Ec says sir decisions taken unanimously by full commission and election commissioners. It also denied the claim that sandhu and joshi wrote to the cabinet secretary to flag concerns over policy matters or it processes. Sir has been implemented in 20 states and uts and is under way in 12 others.

Article Title: SIR row: Congress' Khera questions EC over Form 6, says Bengal & Bihar polls ‘illegal’
Article Text:
EC issues clarification on SIR

Questions Form 6 changes

What is the Form 6 row?

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Pawan Khera on Sunday questioned the Election Commission 's response to concerns over Form 6, claiming that the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was based on a change to the form that could not have been made without amending the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.Speaking to news agency PTI, Khera said the rules could not be changed without being amended in Parliament and questioned whether the Election Commission had addressed the objections raised by Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi."The 1960 Rules cannot be changed without being amended in Parliament. The biggest point of difference between Sandhu ji and Joshi with Gyanesh Kumar was this, and did we receive the answer to it today?" Khera said.Khera alleged that the SIR exercise was based on an "illegally changed" Form 6 and questioned the validity of elections conducted in Bengal and Bihar on the basis of the exercise."The entire SIR is based on a Form 6 that was changed illegally. The SIR that arose from that illegal form has also become illegal. The elections held in Bengal and Bihar based on that illegal SIR have also become illegal. Did we get an answer on this?" he said.The controversy centres on the requirement for new voters to provide details linking themselves or their parents or grandparents to electoral rolls from the previous SIR.According to Indian Express reports, Election Commissioners Joshi and Sandhu had objected to incorporating the requirement into Form 6, arguing that the statutory form could not be altered without an amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960.The Election Commission, however, has maintained that there was "no change" to Form 6 and that the SIR-related requirement was an additional declaration prescribed under its SIR orders. The poll panel has also said the declaration attached to Form 6 for SIR had been upheld by the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: Congress leader pawan khera questions the election commission's response to concerns over form 6. He claims the special intensive revision (sir) of electoral rolls was based on a change to the form that could not have been made without amending the registration of electors rules, 1960.

Article Title: BJP allies close ranks, flay opposition for 'undermining democracy'
Article Text:
Andhra Pradesh CM N Chandrababu Naidu backed the Election Commission’s statement on SIR, saying it reaffirmed the integrity and credibility of constitutional institutions

NEW DELHI: BJP's allies on Saturday closed ranks to hit out at opposition, with TDP chief and Andhra Pradesh CM N Chandrababu Naidu saying EC's statement reaffirmed "the integrity and credibility of our constitutional institutions" and ended "misconceptions" around it. "Attempts to undermine global confidence in India's democratic framework for short-term political gains are deeply unfortunate," he said, urging opposition to accept wins and losses with grace.LJP (Ram Vilas)'s Chirag Paswan said opposition is spreading confusion and questioned why it keeps silent on states where it has formed govt.JDU member Sanjay Jha said rising frustration over poll defeats have led opposition to spread propaganda to undermine the democracy.Shiv Sena's Eknath Shinde said Congress keeps mum when it wins but attacks EC when it loses. The united stand came a day after some allies had pressed EC to clarify concerns raised in media reports.
Article Summary: Andhra pradesh cm n chandrababu naidu backed the election commission’s statement on sir. He said it reaffirmed the integrity and credibility of constitutional institutions. The united stand came a day after some allies had pressed ec to clarify concerns raised in media reports.

Article Title: Congress owes nation a public apology: Nabin after EC statement
Article Text:
BJP president Nitin Nabin accused the Congress and its allies of misleading the public over the SIR process, citing the Election Commission’s statement that decisions on SIR were taken unanimously.

NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the Election Commission 's statement, BJP Saturday said it has exposed Congress and its allies as their attack on the poll body was nothing but a continuation of their tactic of shifting blame for their shrinking popular support in elections and demanded their apology.BJP president Nitin Nabin said, "Opposition has once again been exposed for misleading the public on SIR. EC has made it clear that every decision relating to the SIR was taken unanimously by the full commission. Yet, Congress chose to build its allegations around a manufactured lie and attack our constitutional bodies."Nabin noted that opposition has no complaint when it wins but raises questions when it loses.He said, "The hypocrisy is evident. When the same electoral process delivers victories to Congress and its allies, including in states like Keralam and Tamil Nadu, its credibility is readily accepted. But when the people's mandate goes against them elsewhere, they question the very institutions that conduct those elections. Democracy cannot be respected selectively."Those who have repeatedly undermined India's democratic framework for political survival owe the nation an honest reckoning and a public apology, Nabin said.BJP's Ravi Shankar Prasad said the poll panel's statement has made it clear that Rahul had levelled unfounded and shameful allegations. "He and Congress are blaming the Election Commission for their political failures by levelling baseless allegations against a constitutional institution. Today, their web of lies stands exposed yet again," Prasad said.He claimed that the EC statement has made it clear that the Indian Express story was "factually incorrect".
Article Summary: Bjp president nitin nabin accused the congress and its allies of misleading the public over the sir process. He cited the election commission’s statement that decisions on sir were taken unanimously. Nabin noted that opposition has no complaint when it wins but raises questions when it loses.
